intro: This zone takes in three neighbouring colonies of the new city on the left bank of the Tawi: Gandhi Nagar, Nanak Nagar and Shastri Nagar. Together they make a compact patch for home tuition, because the colonies share borders and a tutor living in one can usually teach in the other two without spending long on a main road. Gandhi Nagar is the commercial heart of the group, with specialised markets that the city's master plan singles out, while Nanak Nagar and Shastri Nagar are quieter residential wards. Jammu Tawi railway station sits close by, which helps anyone travelling in by train.

Homes vary more than the colony names suggest. Gandhi Nagar has single-storey government housing next to private houses and a few newer flats; Nanak Nagar is largely independent houses on plotted lanes with some builder floors and small apartment buildings; Shastri Nagar mixes houses with flats, two-bedroom homes being the commonest size there. For a parent, that means the first visit works differently from street to street. A tutor walks up to the door of a plotted house, gives a name at the entrance to a block of flats, and may be stopped at the government quarters, so say which applies before the demo.

Travel inside the zone is short, but the roads that feed it are busy. An elevated road into Gandhi Nagar and the Jewel Chowk link to the old city carry much of the traffic, and the flyover being built from Satwari Chowk to Last Morh means diversions for now, so weekday slots before the evening market rush are easiest to keep. When you ask NXTutors for a tutor, it looks first in your own colony, then at tutors who travel into this zone, then across Jammu, then online. You receive two or three matched tutors, see each fee before a free first demo, and can switch later at no cost.
faqs: Can one tutor cover Gandhi Nagar, Nanak Nagar and Shastri Nagar?

Yes, often. The three colonies share borders, so a tutor based in any of them can take on homes in the other two with only short trips, and a loop road joins Gandhi Nagar and Shastri Nagar with Nai Basti and the highway. Ask the tutor at the demo which colonies they already teach in.
Which part of this zone is busiest in the evening?

The market roads around Gandhi Nagar. Its specialised markets draw shoppers from across the city, and the flyover works between Satwari Chowk and Last Morh add diversions, so a class that starts before the evening rush, or a tutor who comes from inside Nanak Nagar or Shastri Nagar, keeps timings steady.
Is the railway station useful for tutors coming to this zone?

Yes, for tutors travelling from further away. Jammu Tawi railway station is close to all three colonies, so a tutor arriving by train can finish the trip by auto. Most local tutors still ride a two-wheeler, which is the simpler choice for a class held at the same time every weekday.
How does NXTutors handle fees for families in this zone?

Each tutor sets a fee, and you see it before the free first demo. Across NXTutors, most home-tuition sessions fall between ₹800 and ₹2,500 an hour; Classes 11–12, IB/IGCSE and JEE/NEET sit toward the upper end; specialists for IB HL or JEE Advanced can charge more.

intro: The eastern half of the left bank is the city's sector country. Trikuta Nagar was laid out by the Jammu Development Authority in numbered sectors, and Channi Himmat, a Housing Board colony, follows the same idea, so addresses here read like coordinates: sector first, then house. Further east, Channi Rama and Bathindi are newer and less regular, with lanes still filling in and blocks of flats appearing among the houses. When the municipal limits were extended, they reached Channi Himmat and Narwal Bala on this side, which explains why the zone feels like a city edge that has since been built up.

For home tuition, the housing split decides how the first visit goes. In the older sectors almost every home is an independent house on a plot, so a tutor parks outside and rings the bell. In Bathindi and parts of Channi Rama, apartment buildings may want a visitor to sign in, and a tutor new to the area can lose time hunting for an unmarked lane. Two-bedroom homes are the most sought-after size in Channi Rama, a sign that many families there live in flats rather than houses. The local shopping areas inside the sectors make good meeting points to give a tutor.

Jammu Tawi railway station is close to Trikuta Nagar, and the master plan lists a road from the station along the canal to the NH-44 bypass through this zone, as well as a link from Bhatindi Morh towards Sunjwan and Sainik Colony. In practice tutors come by two-wheeler or auto, and the junctions near the station and the bypass set the pace at peak hours. NXTutors starts with tutors who live in your own sector or colony, then those who travel into the zone, then the rest of Jammu, then online. You get two or three matched tutors, a free first demo with each, fees shown upfront and free switching.
faqs: Why do families in Trikuta Nagar and Channi Himmat give sector numbers?

Because both colonies are planned in numbered sectors. Trikuta Nagar runs from Sector 1 to Sector 9 with a Sector 5A, and Channi Himmat has its own numbered sectors, so a sector and house number take a tutor almost to the gate. Newer Channi Rama and Bathindi are better served by a map pin.
Which parts of this zone have the most flats?

Bathindi and Channi Rama. Bathindi has many new flats alongside houses, and Channi Rama keeps adding homes, with two-bedroom configurations the most sought after. Expect a gate register in some of these buildings, while the older sectors of Trikuta Nagar and Channi Himmat are mostly independent houses where the tutor comes to the door.
Is the NH-44 bypass useful for tutors coming into this zone?

Yes. It runs along the zone's eastern edge, and roads from Trikuta Nagar and from Channi Himmat's Sectors 4 and 7 reach it, so tutors living on the highway side can come in without passing the station area. Junctions on the bypass are busy at office hours, so plan slots around them.
If a tutor in this zone does not work out, what can we do?

Ask NXTutors for another match; switching is free. You begin with two or three tutors, closest to your sector first, and each gives a free first demo, so you can compare teaching styles before choosing. Every tutor's fee is visible to you before the demo is booked, too.

intro: The south and south-east of Jammu, where the national highway enters the city, form this zone: Kunjwani around its busy chowk, Greater Kailash a little further in, and the large plotted spread of Sainik Colony towards Chowadhi and Sunjwan. Kunjwani Chowk is where the Pathankot and Bishnah roads meet the city and where the NH bypass along the eastern side begins, crossing the Tawi to join the Srinagar road north of the city. Much of the zone's character comes from the highway: showrooms and shops along the main road, homes in the lanes behind, and residential colonies set back on either side.

Housing varies within a short stretch. Sainik Colony is mainly independent houses on plots, split into two municipal wards, with an Extension where plots are still being built on, so newer addresses there may not show on a map yet. Greater Kailash mixes houses with apartment buildings that sometimes keep a visitor register, and many of its homes have shops within walking distance. In Kunjwani the homes sit in lanes off the highway, near the Gangyal industrial estate, so the main task for a tutor is finding the right turning rather than getting through a gate. Plan the first visit with that in mind.

Two railway stations, Bari Brahmana and Jammu Tawi, are the nearest, but a home tutor here nearly always comes by road. The four-lane Kunjwani–Satwari flyover being completed by the national highways authority should make trips towards Satwari and Gandhi Nagar easier once it opens, and Greater Kailash Chowk is marked in the master plan as needing a grade separator, so class times matter. NXTutors looks first for tutors living in your colony, then in this zone, then elsewhere in Jammu, then online. You receive two or three matched tutors and see each fee before the free first demo; changing tutor later is free.
faqs: Do tutors in this zone mostly travel along the highway?

Yes. NH-44 connects Kunjwani, Greater Kailash and Sainik Colony with each other and with the rest of Jammu, so most tutors arrive by two-wheeler or car along it. A tutor who lives inside the zone can skip the junctions at office hours, which helps weekday classes start on time.
When will the Kunjwani–Satwari flyover open?

We do not give a date. The four-lane flyover over Satwari Chowk is being completed by the national highways authority; until it opens, plan classes as if the junction will be busy, and check the current route with the tutor before the demo so the first class is not delayed.
Is a new road planned that will help Sainik Colony families?

Yes, a link road is planned from the Sainik Colony junction to NH-44 at Purmandal Chowk via Chowadi, and the master plan also proposes a link from Bhatindi Morh towards Sainik Colony through Sunjwan. Neither changes how tutors travel today, so share a map pin for Extension addresses.
Will NXTutors suggest online tutors for families in this zone?

Yes, after the nearest home tutors. NXTutors lists two or three tutors, starting with those in your colony and the rest of the zone, and adds online tutors when a specialist subject teacher lives across the city. Each one offers a free first demo, with the fee shown in advance.

intro: On the right bank of the Tawi, this zone joins the oldest part of Jammu with two long-settled residential areas and one of its fast-growing edges. The old city covers neighbourhoods such as Purani Mandi, Pacca Danga, Fattu Chowgan, Kanak Mandi and Gumat, where the master plan notes narrow alleys opening into squares. Rehari Colony and Bakshi Nagar lie beyond the core, each split into two municipal wards. Sidhra, on the north-eastern side where NH-44 runs along the river below the Shivalik foothills, is where new houses and apartment buildings are going up, with a satellite township proposed around it and Majeen.

Housing follows age. In the old city, homes are older houses packed along lanes, and the front door opens straight onto the lane. Rehari and Bakshi Nagar are mostly houses on established lanes, built up over many years, with shops nearby. Sidhra is the exception: its apartment complexes may register visitors at the gate, and its newer roads may be unfamiliar to tutors from the old side. For a parent, the practical step is the same everywhere in the zone: give the tutor one precise landmark, whether a square, a chowk or a shop, and a phone number before the first class.

Getting around is a matter of lanes, bridges and market hours. Raghunath Bazar, Kanak Mandi Road and Residency Road crowd up when the markets are busy; the Rehari bridge road and Bakshi Nagar's link to Akhnoor Road connect the residential areas; and Sidhra has its own bridge to the old city as well as the bypass to the south. Tutors who live on this bank need not cross the river, so a match from the same side keeps lessons regular. NXTutors suggests two or three tutors, nearest first and then across the zone, Jammu and online, with each fee visible before a free first demo and free switching afterwards.
faqs: Should an old city tutor come by car or two-wheeler?

A two-wheeler, nearly always. The old layout of narrow alleys and small squares leaves little space for a car, and some lanes are easiest on foot for the last stretch. Tutors coming from Rehari or Bakshi Nagar can reach the core without using the river bridges, which keeps the trip simple.
How is Sidhra different from the rest of this zone?

It is newer and still growing. While the old city, Rehari and Bakshi Nagar are long-settled lanes of houses, Sidhra has fresh houses and apartment buildings, a proposed satellite township with Majeen and Rangoura, and NH-44 running through it. Plan for gate registration there, and consider online lessons for specialist subjects.
Can a tutor from Talab Tillo teach in Bakshi Nagar or Rehari?

Usually, yes. Bakshi Nagar borders Talab Tillo and its road links with Akhnoor Road, while Rehari sits close to Janipur and Bakshi Nagar. So tutors from the neighbouring Janipur & Akhnoor Road zone can often teach here without crossing the river, and NXTutors includes them after the most local tutors.
How does NXTutors widen the search for an old city family?

Step by step. It starts with tutors living in your neighbourhood, then those who travel into the Old City & Sidhra zone, then the rest of Jammu, then online. You see two or three matched tutors with their fees, and the first class with each of them is a free demo at home.

intro: North and west of the old city, along the foothills and out towards Akhnoor Road, lie Janipur, Roop Nagar, Paloura and Talab Tillo. The Jammu Development Authority developed colonies at Janipur and Roop Nagar and has a layout plan for Paloura, so much of this zone is plotted housing in planned layouts. Janipur alone is split into four municipal wards and Paloura into three, which gives a sense of how large these residential areas are. Talab Tillo, bordered by Bohri, Canal Road and Bakshi Nagar, is the zone's commercial anchor, with banks, shops and eateries gathered around its chowk.

Most families in this zone live in independent houses, from older homes on settled lanes in Talab Tillo to the newer plotted colonies of Paloura and New Janipur. That makes doorstep arrival normal, and the bigger challenge is direction: plotted lanes can look alike, and newer ones are not always marked. Roop Nagar has a planned layout with a local shopping area that works well as a meeting landmark, and Janipur has markets within walking distance of many homes. Where a lane is hard to find, a map pin sent before the demo is worth more than a long description of the route.

The roads that matter are Janipur Road towards Amphalla Chowk, Sarwal Road from Rehari Chungi to Paloura Chowk, and the link roads from Akhnoor Road and Janipur Road into Paloura Chowk. Minibuses and autos run along them, but tutors here mostly use two-wheelers, and evening traffic decides which class times work. Because the colonies connect so closely, a tutor from one usually reaches the others easily. NXTutors looks first in your own colony, then the zone, then the city, then online, and offers two or three matched tutors, each with the fee visible before a free first demo; switching later is free.
faqs: Which colonies in this zone are planned layouts?

Janipur, Roop Nagar and Paloura. The Development Authority developed colonies at Janipur and Roop Nagar and has a layout plan for Paloura, so much of the housing is plotted. Talab Tillo is older and more mixed, with settled lanes and newer plotted colonies around a busy commercial chowk.
Do tutors in this zone need a car?

Rarely. A two-wheeler handles narrow plotted lanes and tight parking far more easily, and autos and minibuses are easy to find around Talab Tillo and Janipur. Jammu Tawi railway station is on the other bank of the river, so the train helps only tutors coming from further away.
Which part of this zone has shops closest to homes?

Talab Tillo, around its chowk, where banks, shops and eateries cluster; Janipur also has markets within walking distance of many homes, and Roop Nagar has its own shopping area. These make clear landmarks to give a tutor, though the chowk itself is crowded in the evening.
How many tutors will a family in this zone be offered?

Two or three. NXTutors puts tutors from your own colony first, then others who teach across Janipur, Roop Nagar, Paloura and Talab Tillo, then the rest of Jammu and online. Each tutor's fee is shown before a free first demo, and you can switch later free of charge.
